Definition: from G3844 and G5083; to inspect alongside, i.e. note insidiously or scrupulously:--observe, watch.
BiblicalUsage: Paratereo means to watch closely, to inspect with intent, often to accuse. The Pharisees watch Jesus in Mark 3:2 and Luke 6:7 to see whether He will heal on the sabbath, and in Luke 20:20 they send spies to watch Him, hoping to catch Him in His words. Paul turns the word back on the Galatians in Galatians 4:10, where they observe days and months and times and years, watching the calendar as if the calendar could save them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there are two kinds of watching in the Bible: the watching that waits to accuse, and the watching that waits on God. The Pharisees did the first, and it blinded them to the healing in front of them. That is why I hold that I should watch my own heart more closely than I watch other people's faults.
